parties.petitioner: M/s. Sree Surya Developers and Promoters

summary: The appeals arose from a challenge to a High Court judgment allowing an appeal against the trial court's rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) CPC, which held that the suit to set aside a compromise decree was barred under Order XXIII Rule 3A CPC. The appellant contended that the suit was impermissible due to the bar under Order XXIII Rule 3A, while the High Court remanded the matter, citing failure to consider Order XXXII (minor's protection) Rules 1–7. The Supreme Court examined whether maintainability was properly addressed and emphasized that courts must reject cleverly drafted pleas circumventing statutory bars.
legal_provisions_cited: Banwari Lal Vs. Chando Devi, (1993) 1 SCC 581
Pushpa Devi Bhagat Vs. Rajinder Singh & Ors., (2006) 5 SCC 566
T. Arivandandam Vs. T.V. Satyapal and Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 467
final_judgment: The appeals were allowed, and the High Court's judgment was set aside, with the Trial Court's order of plaint rejection under Order VII Rule 11(d) CPC reinstated, holding the suit barred under Order XXIII Rule 3A CPC.
